01 / Professional experience · Keylane

Evolving systems.
Preserving what matters.

Most of my professional engineering experience comes from Keylane. I work on mature Java-based insurance platforms, where policy workflows, established business rules, and external integrations need to keep working as the software evolves.

  • Java
  • REST APIs
  • OpenAPI
  • Backwards compatibility
Role
Senior Software Engineer
Domain
Insurance policy management & integrations
Scope
Analysis, implementation, testing, and release preparation
Explore my engineering approach +

The challenge

Modernise a platform built over many years while preserving behaviour that existing users and integrations depend on.

My part

I translate business requests into requirements and acceptance criteria, analyse existing contracts, design and implement changes, and work with colleagues on review and release preparation.

Designing the contract

Authentication, authorisation, request and response models, HTTP errors, API versioning, and OpenAPI documentation all form part of the design. Compatibility planning includes existing consumers and migration paths.

Building confidence in a change

I reproduce defects through realistic scenarios, trace their root causes, and implement integration and regression coverage. Technical documentation and release notes make the behaviour understandable.

These examples describe my contributions at a general level; company code, customer details, and internal systems remain private.

API modernisation

From SOAP to REST

I help move legacy policy-management interfaces towards REST, analysing established behaviour and designing clearer contracts with security, documentation, and automated tests built in.

Compatible evolution

Change without disruption

I analyse contract and documentation mismatches, plan compatible API changes, and help retire older frontend paths while preserving required routes, permissions, and user journeys.

Quality & investigation

From symptom to root cause

I trace defects across business scenarios, data, APIs, and code. Reproducible cases and integration, regression, and browser tests help verify fixes and protect existing behaviour.

Developer tooling

Better context, better decisions

I contribute to exploratory AI-assisted workflows for bug triage, technical analysis, and reusable engineering handoffs, checking source references and keeping engineering judgement central.

02 / Community software

Private repository

Fusion Almere FC

I’m building a club platform that brings registration, player profiles, and administration together, replacing fragmented spreadsheet workflows with a shared application.

  • Public registration & player portal
  • Role-based administration & member management
  • Java API backed by Supabase Auth and PostgreSQL
  • Java 21
  • Spring Boot
  • Angular
  • Supabase
Explore the club platform +

The challenge

Help players register and manage their profiles while giving club administrators a consistent way to manage members and teams.

My part

I’m building an Angular front end and a Spring Boot REST API with Supabase authentication, database, and storage. Features include registration, profile editing, searchable member records, and team-management services.

An engineering detail

Registration checks for duplicate accounts and records an audit trail. Notification emails are sent after the database transaction commits, avoiding messages for rolled-back changes.

Where it stands

An evolving MVP with a public test deployment on Vercel and Render. Further membership features and payment-import workflows are under active development.

03 / Data & reliability

Private repository

HomeWizard Energy Intelligence

A Java collector and an authenticated React application that turn smart-meter readings into historical insights, making energy use, data quality, and load-shifting options easier to explore.

  • Durable collection with retry and replay
  • Historical imports, coverage, and freshness indicators
  • Measured data kept distinct from modelled scenarios
  • Java
  • React
  • SQLite
  • Supabase
Explore the energy application +

The challenge

Make energy history useful while keeping missing readings and estimates visible. The collector also needs to recover reliably from interruptions.

My part

The project spans HomeWizard API integration, a Java collector, durable local SQLite storage, authenticated Supabase ingestion, and an interface built with React and TypeScript.

An engineering detail

Readings are persisted before upload, then replayed with ingestion that prevents duplicate records. The interface shows coverage and freshness so users can assess the data.

Where it stands

A private hosted application with historical exploration and load-shifting features. Tariff, solar, and battery scenarios continue to evolve, with cost comparisons still in progress.

Explore the Java toolkit +

The challenge

Keep solutions across multiple puzzle years organised, repeatable, and easy to validate as the collection grows.

My part

The repository combines Java solutions with reusable test, tracking, caching, and dashboard utilities. It also includes a Playwright automation pipeline and an AI-assisted workflow using GitHub Copilot.

What to look for

Look at how the tools select unsolved puzzles, check results, and track progress across the collection. This is an ongoing learning and tooling project.

04 / The person behind the work

A different path.
A useful perspective.

Before developing financial software, I worked in the operations it supports.

My path took me from economics and banking operations to postgraduate study in information technology and a career in enterprise software engineering. That experience helps me connect technical decisions with business processes and the people using them.

My approach starts with understanding existing behaviour and what users and integrations depend on. I design for compatibility, implement changes incrementally, automate regression checks, and document the contract so the next engineer can follow the reasoning.
